== EXTRACTION RULES (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task C & §5.2; CODEBOOK.md §§1-9; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, set `value = "cannot_tell"`, `where_found = "not accessible"`, and `comment = "full text not accessible"` for ALL 9 fields, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER copy publication year or country from the citation header when the full paper was not read!
2. IF FULL TEXT IS READABLE:
   - Extract each of the 9 fields strictly from the paper text. Write a field value ONLY if the paper explicitly states it; if not stated in the paper, write `"not reported"` in `value` and explain in `comment`. Never guess or infer from context.
   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).
   - `outcome_flags`: Comma-separated list using ONLY exact `CODEBOOK.md` §5 codes actually studied in the paper (`formal_connection`, `water_access`, `sanitation_access`, `service_coverage`, `service_reliability`, `service_quantity`, `service_quality`, `affordability`, `service_continuity`, `application_success`, `refusal`, `delay`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.
3. `where_found` AND `evidence_quotes`:
   - Every field's `where_found` must give exact PDF page(s), section, and/or table/figure number (e.g. `"PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; Table 1, PDF p. 7"`).

evidence_quotes.quote: Background: Our group conducted a cluster-randomised trial in 100 villages of Orissa, India to measure the impact
The percentage of households with a latrine (completed or under construction) increased from 8% at baseline
Table 2 Awareness of mobilisation activities among intervention and control households (n = 807)

evidence_quotes.criterion: effect estimate on programme and VWSC awareness
evidence_quotes.quote: generally more aware of the Total Sanitation Campaign (91% versus 49%, p < 0.001), VWSCs (51% versus 9%, p < 0.001),
tensions between the NGOs and communities. As a result, implementers decided to provide a subsidy to all

country.comment: Conducted in 100 rural villages across seven blocks of Puri district in the State of Orissa, India.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF p. 3, Results (Study setting)

effect_estimate.comment: Reports both longitudinal latrine construction coverage, cross-arm awareness comparisons from the cluster-randomised villages, and village-level linear regression coefficients within the 50 intervention villages alongside qualitative implementation findings.
effect_estimate.value: Latrine coverage (completed or under construction) in the 50 intervention villages increased from 8% at baseline (October 2010) to 66% in March 2012 (68% among BPL households vs. 61% among APL households; range 54% to 76% across NGOs), while completed latrine coverage rose from 8% to 51% between January 2011 and January 2012 (below the 90% target). In the random 10% household survey (n = 807: 408 intervention, 399 control), intervention households had higher awareness of the Total Sanitation Campaign (91% vs. 49%, p < 0.001), VWSCs (51% vs. 9%, p < 0.001), adolescent girls groups (23% vs. 8%, p < 0.01), wall paintings (44% vs. 7%, p < 0.001), and sanitation home visits in the past 3 months (65% vs. 3%, p < 0.001), but negligible recall of participatory transect walks/mapping (6% vs. 10%, p = 0.04) or wealth ranking (0% vs. 1%, p = 0.09). In village-level linear regressions across the 50 intervention villages, latrine coverage was associated with seeing wall paintings (beta = 0.171, 95% CI: 0.001 to 0.341, p = 0.05), a village motivator home visit in the past month (beta = 0.216, 95% CI: -0.000 to 0.431, p = 0.05 in Table 4; p = 0.02 in text), and >=5 VWSC meetings held (beta = 0.178, 95% CI: 0.010 to 0.346, p = 0.04), with no significant association for participatory mobilisation activities; restricting subsidies to BPL/wealth-ranked poor households caused community tensions that led implementers to extend subsidies to all intervention households.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Results (Latrine construction); PDF p. 7, Results; PDF pp. 8-9, Table 2; PDF p. 9, Discussion; PDF p. 11, Table 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Mixed-methods process evaluation (appraised with MMAT, design ceiling = 2) that directly observed and documented administrative and implementation mechanisms on the ground, including BPL list verification, community tensions over selective poverty-targeted subsidies prompting discretionary universal subsidy extension, complaints following the statutory subsidy raise from Rs 2200 to Rs 3200, VWSC functioning, NGO motivator visits, and election code-of-conduct halts.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 2, Methods; PDF pp. 4-7, Results (Fidelity assessment); PDF p. 9, Discussion; PDF p. 11, Table 4

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines BPL card eligibility verification against Gram Panchayat records (ELIGIBILITY, documentation), wealth-ranking and WaterAid subsidies for non-BPL poor plus discretionary extension of INR 2200 subsidies to all households to avert conflict (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, hardship_exception, discretion), household co-contributions of ~INR 2200 in materials/labour (BURDEN, fees), implementation delays (delay), community complaints over the subsidy increase from Rs 2200 to Rs 3200 and construction disputes (complaint), VWSCs and PRA mobilisation (participation), NGO-local government coordination and 2-month election code-of-conduct halts/local political unrest (political_coordination), and weekly door-to-door NGO village motivator support with construction logistics (bureaucratic_assistance).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, documentation, fees, delay, discretion, hardship_exception, complaint, participation, political_coordination, bureaucratic_assistance
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 3-7, Results (Context, Intervention, Fidelity assessment); PDF p. 5, Table 1; PDF p. 9, Discussion

outcome_flags.comment: Measures household latrine construction/access (sanitation_access), village-level sanitation/latrine coverage (service_coverage), and construction/implementation delays across villages (delay).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 2, Methods; PDF p. 4, Results (Latrine construction); PDF p. 6, Figures 1-2; PDF p. 7, Results; PDF p. 9, Discussion

publication_year.comment: Published 1 August 2014 in BMC Research Notes (2014, 7:486).
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, footer & copyright line; PDF p. 12, publication history

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Although embedded within a 100-village cluster-randomised trial (whose trial protocol and main health trial are reported separately), this paper is a mixed-methods process evaluation combining primary qualitative methods (semi-structured interviews with NGO staff/motivators and community members, review of implementation logs/documents) and primary quantitative methods (repeated direct observations of household latrines, random household and VWSC surveys, and observational village-level linear regressions in the 50 intervention villages), making MMAT the design-matched appraisal tool.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 2-3, Methods

sample_size.comment: Multiple nested samples are explicitly reported for the different components of the mixed-methods process evaluation within the 100-village trial.
sample_size.value: 100 villages (50 intervention villages and 50 control villages); latrine construction observations in 4,699 households (March 2012) and 4,585 households (March 2013); household awareness survey of 807 households (408 intervention and 399 control, 10% random sample); VWSC survey of 170 village water and sanitation committee members across intervention villages (VWSC composition data from 48 villages); plus semi-structured interviews and logbook reviews with NGO staff (25 village motivators and 6 cluster coordinators trained)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 2-4, Methods & Results; PDF p. 6, Figure 1; PDF p. 8, Table 2; PDF p. 10, Table 3

study_design.comment: Process evaluation conducted alongside a cluster-randomised trial, based on the Linnan and Steckler framework, integrating qualitative interviews/document review with quantitative household and VWSC surveys, direct latrine observations every 6-8 weeks, cross-arm t-tests of village proportions, and observational village-level linear regression.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods process evaluation conducted in connection with a cluster-randomised controlled trial (combining document review, semi-structured interviews, longitudinal direct observations of latrine construction, cross-sectional household and VWSC member surveys, and village-level linear regression)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Abstract; PDF pp. 2-3, Methods
